sections.heading: What Are Clear Aligners?
sections.body: Clear aligners are smooth, custom-fabricated plastic trays that move your teeth gradually into position using gentle, controlled pressure. Each tray shifts your teeth incrementally, and you advance through the series until treatment is complete. You wear each set for approximately one to two weeks, then move on to the next.

sections.heading: Who Is a Good Candidate for Clear Aligners?
sections.body: Clear aligners work well for mild to moderate crowding, gaps between teeth, spacing irregularities, and minor bite issues such as a slight overbite or underbite. They are also effective for patients who had orthodontic work in the past and have seen some gradual shifting since. Severe crowding, significant bite discrepancies, or complex jaw alignment concerns may require a different approach. Aligners are also a common preparatory step inside a broader smile makeover, positioning teeth before porcelain veneers or whitening for a more stable final result. Candidacy is confirmed at your consultation with a 3D scan and clinical review of your specific tooth positions.

sections.body: Gum contouring removes or reshapes excess gum tissue so that more of the natural tooth surface becomes visible, improving the overall balance between gums and teeth. sections.heading: How Laser Technology Makes Gum Contouring Gentle and Precise
sections.body: Laser gum contouring is significantly more precise and comfortable than traditional scalpel-based gingivectomy (surgical gum removal), with less bleeding, no sutures in most cases, and faster healing. Local anesthetic is all that is needed during the procedure, and most patients are genuinely surprised by how uneventful the experience turns out to be.

sections.heading: What Are Porcelain Veneers?
sections.body: Porcelain veneers are ultra-thin custom shells bonded to the front surface of your teeth to correct discoloration, chips, gaps, misalignment, and worn enamel.
